newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica co-ops sell 250,000 t yellow maize to Iran.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica co-ops sell 250,000 t yellow maize to Iran.

text.p: South African co-operatives were successful in selling 250,000 tonnes of yellow maize to Iran in the past week, Unie Graan co-operative chairman J Theron said in a statement on Friday.
Theron said the quantity of maize was part of the surplus of yellow maize to be exported this year.
"Several consignments of white and yellow maize have already been sold in advance by the grain co-operatives, for destinations in South America, Japan, Kenia and Mauritius," he said.
Based on the national crop estimate of 8.2 million tonnes, more than 70 percent of the expected export surplus had already been sold by the grain co-operatives and grain traders for export purposes.
Theron said the local grain market was very quiet at present, as processors and buyers were slow to buy given the expected surplus of between one and one-and-a-half million tonnes.
"Should local buyers not make their purchases timeously, they may find that larger quantities will be exported," he said.
